name: Select
hint: Open it with a click or the arrow keys. Watch the highlight travel and the value roll.
description: Dropdown select field for picking one value, or several, from a list of options: a country, a role, a time zone, a status. At rest it matches Text Field (label floating or above, hint and error line, focus ring). The popup springs out of the field, one highlight pill slides between options and stretches on long jumps, the tick draws on the option you pick, and the value rolls into the field in the direction of the move. Grouped options, descriptions, icons, multiple choice, a clear button, loading and empty states. Keyboard and screen-reader behaviour (combobox and listbox roles, arrows, Home / End, typeahead) come from the @base-ui/react package.
intents: pick one option from a dropdown list
choose a country, role or time zone in a form
select field with a long list of options
usage: Use for one value (or several, with `multiple`) out of a list too long to show at once: a country, a role, a time zone, a status. Pass `options` (strings, `{ value, label, description, icon, disabled }`, or groups `{ label, options }`), a `label`, `name` for forms, and either `value` + `onChange(value, option, event)` (controlled) or `defaultValue` (it keeps its own; a form reset returns to it). With `multiple`, `value` is an array and `onChange(values, { value, selected, option }, event)`. Do not use it for two to five short options that fit on screen (use Segmented Control or Radio Group), for actions rather than values (use Dropdown Menu), or for a list people need to type to filter (use Combobox; Command Palette is for commands). It sits in a form beside Text Field: give every field the same `labelPlacement`. `error` shows a message you already have; `required` blocks an empty submit and focuses the field; bump `revealErrors` on every submit to show the required message and shake. `loading` shows skeleton rows while you fetch options; an empty `options` shows `labels.empty`. `clearable` adds a clear button. `renderOption(option, { selected, highlighted, disabled })` and `renderValue(option | options)` swap in your own markup and keep the keyboard behaviour. The popup does not lock page scroll and stays anchored on phones, as Dropdown Menu does. The ref and unknown props (aria-*, data-*) go to the trigger button. Keyboard and screen-reader behaviour come from the @base-ui/react package (install it beside motion).

keyboard.does: Opens the list with the chosen option highlighted.
Chooses the next option starting with that letter without opening the list; repeating a letter cycles through its options.
keyboard.when: on the closed field, not multiple

keyboard.does: Moves the highlight to the next or previous option; a disabled option can be highlighted but not chosen.
Moves the highlight to the first or last option.
Moves the highlight to the next option starting with the letters typed.
Chooses the highlighted option, closes the list and returns focus to the field.
Closes the list without changing the value and returns focus to the field.
Closes the list and moves focus to the next control.
Clears the value and returns focus to the field.

screenReader: The field is a button with role combobox, aria-haspopup="listbox" and aria-expanded, named by `label` (pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` when there is none) and described by `hint` or the error; an error sets aria-invalid. The list is a listbox of options with aria-selected and aria-disabled, in groups named by their label. While `loading` the field and list are aria-busy and a status says `labels.loading`; an empty list's status says `labels.empty`.

dataProps.type: Array<string | number | { value: string | number; label?: node; description?: node; icon?: node; disabled?: boolean } | { label: string; options: Array<string | number | { value: string | number; label?: node; description?: node; icon?: node; disabled?: boolean }> }>
dataProps.description: Strings, { value, label, description?, icon?, disabled? } objects, or groups { label, options: [...] }. A string s is short for { value: s, label: s }. Empty shows labels.empty.
Controlled value (an array with multiple; null for none). Pass it with onChange.
Starting value when uncontrolled; also what a form reset returns to.

dataProps.type: (value: string | number | null | Array<string | number>, detail: { value: string | number; label?: node; description?: node; icon?: node; disabled?: boolean } | null | { value: string | number; selected: boolean; option: { value: string | number; label?: node; description?: node; icon?: node; disabled?: boolean } | null }, event?: Event) => void
dataProps.description: (value, option, event) => void; with multiple (values, { value, selected, option }, event). Also fires on clear and on a form reset that changes the value.
Controlled open state. Pass it with onOpenChange.
Open on first render when uncontrolled.
(open, reason, event) => void. reason: trigger, select, escape, outside, blur, keyboard, resize, other.
An error you already have; shown under the field, announced, and the field shakes once when it arrives.
Bump on every submit: the field marks itself touched, shows the required message if empty, and shakes.
Form field name. A hidden input submits the value (one entry per value with multiple).
Autofill hint for the hidden input, e.g. "country".

dataProps.type: Partial<{ clear: string; empty: node; loading: node; required: node }>
dataProps.description: Copy: { clear: "Clear", empty: "No options", loading: "Loading options", required: "Choose an option" }.

dataProps.type: (option: { value: string | number; label?: node; description?: node; icon?: node; disabled?: boolean }, state: { selected: boolean; highlighted: boolean; disabled: boolean }) => node
dataProps.description: (option, { selected, highlighted, disabled }) => node, the content of one row (the tick stays).

dataProps.type: (chosen: { value: string | number; label?: node; description?: node; icon?: node; disabled?: boolean } | Array<{ value: string | number; label?: node; description?: node; icon?: node; disabled?: boolean }>) => node
dataProps.description: (option | options) => node, what the field shows for the chosen value(s).
Goes to the trigger <button>, for focus().
Any other attribute (id, aria-*, data-*) goes to the field's <button>. className and style go to the root <div> and are merged with the component's own.

example:
<Select
  label="Time zone"
  name="tz"
  autoComplete="off"
  placeholder="Choose a time zone"
  options={[
    { label: "Europe", options: ["Europe/Lisbon", "Europe/Berlin"] },
    { label: "Americas", options: [
      { value: "America/Bogota", label: "Bogotá", description: "UTC−5" },
      { value: "America/Toronto", label: "Toronto", description: "UTC−5, DST" },
    ] },
  ]}
  value={tz}
  onChange={(value) => setTz(value)}
  required
/>
